M14.0.SPEC (#419) — toml completeness classification. Every public NAMED node type of the pinned wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm is in exactly one bucket. The grammar exposes 20 nodeTypeForId slots but only 19 DISTINCT names: `escape_sequence` is declared twice, which is a grammar quirk rather than two node types. MEASURED, not restated (2026-10-09, commit 840bffea9): enumerating wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm through web-tree-sitter's Language API gives 66 node-type slots, of which 20 are NAMED and 19 are distinct named names — exactly the claim above, with the anonymous punctuation tokens making up the remaining 46 slots (44 distinct). ERROR and MISSING are injected by this gate for EVERY language because the wasm ABI does not list them; neither occurs for this grammar and both are silent here. Silence is guilt: a type in no bucket fails section A, and a type the wasm no longer produces is a stale row and also fails. That rule bites hardest on the four DATETIME types — none appears anywhere in cargo's 684 files, so their handling is pinned by FIXTURE rather than by the corpus, and a corpus-only lane would have classified them by assumption and called it coverage. SECTION D IS RED AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. The gate requires >=2 distinct `evidenceClass` values and TOML has exactly ONE: every edge it emits is `structural`. YAML, the closest config-format precedent, pins four and legitimately so — a merge key is an inference, an anchor is a reference, an `!include` is a fetch. TOML has none of those constructs: no merge, no anchor, no alias, no include, no import, no reference of any kind. Its whole graph is a nesting the document literally writes. Both routes to a second tier are dishonest and neither was taken: emitting a `uses` edge for a path-shaped string imports ecosystem knowledge about which keys are paths in which tool into a format that defines no references, and tagging an edge to an IMPLIED parent as `inferred` points at a target that is deliberately not a symbol, where an edge to a non-existent node is the unresolvable-identity defect. D stays red until the gate grows a documented single-tier allowance or TOML grows a construct that earns one. E and F are the canonical F5 ceremony, exactly as for html.

handled_verified.note: Twenty-one types, each read in src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts and each pinned. `ERROR` is handled for the corpus reason recorded on the internal_silent side, and the analyzer now walks for recovery nodes itself — REPORTED at the node's OWN span, BYPASSED, and everything AROUND it still published. It had been pushing no diagnostics at all, so the "reported" half of the contract was entirely the engine's: a contract resting on a caller is not a contract, which is the same blindness the svelte lane had in the opposite direction. `children`, not `namedChild`, because the expected token of a MISSING node can be anonymous. Pinned by `toml/malformed-and-rejected` and `toml/error-node-becomes-symbol`. DECLARED CONSEQUENCE OF THE BYPASS, measured rather than assumed: a key whose VALUE fails to parse is not published. The whole `key = invalid-value` pair sits inside the ERROR, and the walk does not descend into one, so `invalid-section.key` is absent from a document whose table and every earlier key are present. Measured over the whole pool this costs exactly TWO symbols in TWO files, both cargo's own invalid-manifest fixtures. It is declared rather than repaired because recovering the key means inferring table scope from POSITION inside a region the parser marked unreadable — the ERROR sits at document level, so ownership would have to come from "the last header before this offset", and a wrong guess attaches a real key to the wrong table. Two symbols in two intentionally-broken files does not justify that risk, and the alternative is not silence: the file is reported with a parse error at the key's own line. DECLARED, ZERO CORPUS OCCURRENCES: an unterminated header such as `[bad` is recovered by the grammar into a real `table` node whose header children include an ERROR, and a following genuine header is nested inside that ERROR. Read naively the analyzer would publish the invented table and lose the real one. Measured across all 743 files this shape occurs ZERO times, so no behaviour is changed on the strength of a synthetic input — the same discipline that removed the values-as-symbols mutant rather than fixing it, on the grounds that the measured enter state is stronger evidence than a stand-in. It is recorded so a future corpus that does contain the shape inherits the decision instead of rediscovering it.

internal_silent.note: MISSING and `comment` are two types that correctly emit nothing and need no analyzer read. `comment` is a literal: a comment is not an identity, and TOML has no block-comment form, so a `#` line contributes nothing to the graph. MISSING holds across the whole 743-file pool — zero MISSING nodes, and it is a property of this grammar that a recovery node is always a full ERROR rather than an inserted token. ERROR WAS HERE AND WAS WRONG, and the correction is recorded because the reasoning that put it here is the exact trap the svelte lane fell into on the same day. This note previously read "NEITHER OCCURS for this grammar", on the evidence of TWELVE HAND-MADE MALFORMED DOCUMENTS. The corpus was never measured. Measuring it: 2 of 743 files (0.27%) carry an ERROR node — `cargo/tests/testsuite/cargo_add/invalid_manifest/{in,out}/Cargo.toml`, cargo's own deliberately-invalid manifest fixtures, where `key = invalid-value` is a bare word where TOML requires a value. Two hand-made malformed documents and 743 real ones disagreed, and the real ones were right. ERROR now sits in handled_verified, and the analyzer reports it itself rather than leaving the whole contract to the engine.

gaps.missing: `references` for the Cargo workspace-inheritance shape: `x.workspace = true` says this key's value is declared by the workspace manifest, and the analyzer's alias pass does not walk it, so these sites emit no edge
gaps.measured: 1,269 sites in 138 documents over the 1,485 admitted .toml files of the whole corpus (shape: a pair whose leaf is `workspace` with the boolean value true). The brief carried 1,267 and the in-tree applicability audit 1,269; the whole-corpus count through the production path is 1,269, and the raw run is committed at validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/census-whole-corpus.json under workspaceInheritance
gaps.consequence: this is the SAME ontology type as the 167 alias `references` edges the lane does emit (Gradle version catalogues, resolvedBy=final-segment), so the type's corpus coverage is partial rather than absent; it is recorded here as an OPEN item with a size and NOT folded into the coverage number, because a blocker quietly absorbed into a ratio is a number nobody can check
gaps.why_not_fixed: the alias pass resolves a key whose VALUE is the name of another key in the same document; `workspace = true` is a boolean that defers to a DIFFERENT document, and resolving it means locating and reading that document's manifest — a cross-file resolution the analyzer deliberately does not do from a pure AST worker (see the `imports` note in src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts on why paths are emitted unresolved). Not attempted without a design ruling; recorded, not guessed

gaps.measured: Whole admitted population (1,485 .toml files / 77 repos, 0 parse failures), `npx tsx script/m14/residual-gate.ts --lane toml`: imports 331 edges — 321 carry `importProjectFile` and the project CONFIRMS all 321 (extOK 321, extFAIL 0, ext? 0), 10 name a directory that does not exist. Every unresolved edge is LOCATED in validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/residual-whole-population.txt (whole population, production path `parseFile`, shared counting rule `classifyEdge`; it reproduces all thirty compared gate columns exactly). THE THIRTEEN WERE NOT ONE CAUSE, and the previous text here said every one was cargo's own `cargo_add` fixture — a MEASUREMENT REFUTED THAT: 8 declared Cargo's `base =` on the same inline table, and 3 of those resolve through the nearest `.cargo/config.toml` `[path-bases]` entry (Cargo `src/workspace/parser/mod.rs:2456-2483`, `lookup_path_base`) to a manifest the project really carries — FIXED 2026-10-13, unresolved 13 -> 10 and extOK 318 -> 321 over the SAME population, with the analyzer's `imports` edge count UNCHANGED at 331. The remaining 10 are 9 cargo `cargo_add` fixtures under `out/` (whose `.cargo/config.toml` is absent from the fixture tree, so the base is undefined and Cargo itself would refuse) and Pkg.jl `test/test_packages/WorkspacePathResolution/SubProjectA/Project.toml:9` (`SubProjectB = {path = "SubProjectB"}`)
gaps.instrument: src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts `dependencyFileClaim` (+ the `[path-bases]` fallback `pathBaseCandidates`) gated on the manifest's presence; measured by script/m14/residual-gate.ts TABLE 1 and independently by validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/residual-whole-population.mts over the whole population
gaps.consequence: residual is 10 of 25,531 edges (0.04%), all 10 named and located rather than hidden. They are NOT marked external or given a claim the project would refute: a file claim on any of them REFUTES (measured over the whole population — `verifyFileClaim` 0 verified / 10 refuted, which would take extFAIL 0 -> 10), and a bare-target external marker would verify 5 of the 10 VACUOUSLY (measured — `verifyExternalClaim` verifies exactly the bare identifiers the same rule has already found declare nothing, which is HANDOFF §5l's laundering vector run rather than quoted). The honest statement about a dependency on a directory that does not exist is that it names nothing here
gaps.why_not_fixed: the target directory genuinely does not exist beside the declaring manifest, so no true file claim can verify. RUN FALSIFIER, whole population: 0 of the 10 name a manifest on disk or in the admitted list under the standard spellings, and 0 would receive a file claim. THE STRONGEST ARM WAS ALSO RUN AND IS REFUTED BY THE LANGUAGE'S OWN RULE: folded one level up (the "the path is relative to the workspace root" reading), 5 of the 10 DO name a real manifest — Pkg.jl's `SubProjectB` sibling and cargo's `out/dependency` — and claiming those would VERIFY while naming a DIFFERENT unit than the document means, because Pkg.jl `src/Operations.jl:3295-3301` joins a `[sources]` path with `dirname(project_file)` and Cargo resolves a `path` against the manifest that declares it (HANDOFF §5h: a wrong edge the arbiter cannot see). Left as an honest gap with a count. ROUND 2 (2026-10-13) ran the FULL PER-EDGE BATTERY and the gap is a PROVEN BOUNDARY, not a backlog: for all 10 edges eight candidate spellings were folded and stat'd from disk (`residual-whole-population.txt`, `--battery`), and every spelling that names a real file is refused — A5/A7 are cargo's test-harness snapshot layout (`assert_ui().subset_matches(out, project_root)` in each fixture's `mod.rs`), A6 is a project-wide name coincidence (§5h), and the one edge whose dependency is genuinely declared (Pkg.jl's `SubProjectB`, listed in the workspace root's `[workspace] projects`) needs a MEMBERSHIP claim kind the arbiter does not have. The `[path-bases]` rule (A3) fires on NONE of the 10, which is the control that says the fix took exactly what it could

decisions.question: Should the analyzer decode a quoted key's escapes by WALKING its `escape_sequence` child nodes, or by decoding the quoted_key's own text in pure-String?
decisions.ruling: RULED: decode the PARENT'S TEXT, in pure-String, and never walk `escape_sequence`. The two are equivalent by construction — an escape_sequence node's text is exactly the escape sequence its parent contains — so walking the children would buy nothing and cost a second pass over every quoted key. It would also put the lane's no-regex rule under pressure: the natural way to express a decode is a replacement pattern, and that rule exists because every regex literal is one more thing to audit for backtracking. The decode handles the escapes TOML defines in a key (\n, \t, \r, \", \\, \uXXXX) and passes an UNKNOWN escape through with its backslash rather than dropping it, because silently discarding half a key would invent a different identity. Measured: `"a\u0062c"` resolves to the single key `abc`, and a literal-string key takes a pure slice because a literal string has no escapes at all.
decisions.consequence: `escape_sequence` is classified HERE rather than as handled, so the type is accounted for exactly once and the reason it is not walked is on the record rather than being invisible.

coverage._from: DERIVATION. implemented = the three types the production path fires over the WHOLE admitted population (construct-census, commit 840bffea9; raw run validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/census-whole-corpus.json): contains 25,033 edges / 1,474 files, imports 331 / 153, references 167 / 5. The 120-file firing log reads only `contains:882 imports:16` and marks references SILENT — a stride sample that invents an absence — so this block follows the census, not the sample. The six exclusions are grammar-absence, each carrying a count: 0 of the 19 named node types of the pinned grammar (66 node-type slots, 20 named slots, 1 duplicate named slot) can carry the construct, and the corpus corroborates with 0 occurrences or 0 referents. `exports` is deliberately NOT excluded: the lane's own applicability audit (self-test 14/14, positive control fired 167/167 aliases) reports it UNVERIFIED and exits 1 — 174 publish-shaped key sites exist (118 string-valued: module, publish, main, public, exposed), and nothing in this lane MEASURES that TOML cannot express the relation, so it stays IN the denominator as an unimplemented applicable type (a gap) rather than being promoted to grammar-absence. ARITHMETIC: 3 implemented + 0 corpus-unexercised + 1 gap (exports) = 4 applicable = 10 − 6 grammar-absence − 0 unclassified. RELATED OPEN ITEM, not folded into this ratio: TOML-G1 — the workspace-inheritance half of `references`, 1,269 sites in 138 documents. AND `exports` STAYS IN THE DENOMINATOR, with its size re-measured 2026-10-13 over the same 1,485-file population (validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/residual-whole-population.mts --exports): 174 publish-surface key sites, 118 string-valued, 0 whose value names a declaration in the SAME document (the census's `referentSites`, reproduced by an independent walk), 1 whose value names a declaration ANYWHERE in the project (`docs/netlify.toml publish = "build"` — a name coincidence, not a publication), and 0 values ending in `.toml`. The lane's admitted population is `.toml` alone, so a file claim cannot verify such a target and a bare-target external claim is unfalsifiable (HANDOFF §5l); the completion score therefore remains 3 of 4 applicable types, not 3/3.

_implemented_measured._unit: edges published through the production path over the WHOLE 1,485-file toml population (77 repos, 0 failures) — validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/census-whole-corpus.json, `relationshipTypes`. `files` is the count of distinct files the type appeared in, as the census records it.
